title: Edmund Hall's father and the carnival bands from upriver
summary: Hall's father played in the Onward band; bands from the country came down to win carnival prizes in red uniforms.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: So, and they used to come down here every carnival didn't play. And every carnival would come, and every time they come down here they would win the prize. Is that with your father's band? My father's band. Every time they come down here they used to wear a red, a red uniform, red outfit you know. So I used to come down here every year carnival they would come down. For eleven years when you used to have carnival they didn't have enough bands. They used to send off and get band different parts you know. Sure. You know what I mean? Different part of the country you know. Because they used to have a lot of parades. And like, not like today you see. So, well they come down here and he, well he played a long time. But after that the band, broke up you know what I mean? Band broke up. Then the fellas, fellas they organized, they had a orchestra. They had an orchestra you see. Not my daddy. He didn't have no, they didn't have no orchestra, not him. But Marshall Lawrence, he had an orchestra. He played the violets. He was, he managed the band, lead the band. And the fella used to play the trumpet. Well he got drowned.
